title: Identifying the Inflationary Potential
bottleneck: Inflation fits the data beautifully, yet hundreds of potentials reproduce the observed spectral index and tensor limits; Planck's constraints rule out the simplest monomial models but leave a vast viable landscape. There is no known observation short of primordial B-modes that could pick out the true potential. The Lyth bound ties observable gravitational waves to super-Planckian field excursions, which effective field theory struggles to control.
why_it_blocks: Without the potential, inflation remains a paradigm without a theory, disconnected from particle physics.
current_state: Planck 2018 plus BICEP/Keck set r < 0.036; next-generation CMB-S4 targets r ~ 0.001, which would kill or confirm large-field models. A non-detection of B-modes down to r ~ 0.001 would eliminate the entire large-field class, a major culling of the model space.
